events.title: U.S. Congress Passes the Embargo Act
events.description: At the urging of President Thomas Jefferson, Congress passed the Embargo Act. It forbade American ships from trading with foreign countries. Jefferson hoped to pressure Britain and France to respect U.S. neutrality during the Napoleonic Wars.
events.significance: The embargo badly hurt American merchants and ports, and it proved deeply unpopular. It is a well-known early test of economic pressure as a foreign-policy tool, and it was repealed in 1809.

events.title: Birth of Giacomo Puccini
events.description: The composer Giacomo Puccini was born in Lucca, Italy, into a long line of musicians. He went on to write some of the best-loved operas ever staged, including La Bohème, Tosca, Madama Butterfly and Turandot.
events.significance: Puccini carried Italian opera into the modern era. His works are still among the most performed in the world.

events.title: Savannah Falls to Sherman
events.description: Union General William Tecumseh Sherman captured Savannah, Georgia, at the end of his March to the Sea. He offered the city to President Abraham Lincoln as a Christmas gift.
events.significance: The capture deepened the Confederacy's economic and military collapse and showed that Union forces could cross the Southern heartland. It helped bring the Civil War to its close a few months later.

events.title: A 'Living Fossil' Is Found: The Coelacanth
events.description: Marjorie Courtenay-Latimer, curator of a small museum in East London, South Africa, noticed an unusual fish in the catch of a local trawler. It turned out to be a coelacanth, a lineage thought to have died out about 70 million years ago.
events.significance: It was one of the most celebrated zoological discoveries of the 20th century. It showed that species once known only from fossils can still survive.

events.title: Ceaușescu's Regime Falls in Romania
events.description: After a week of bloody demonstrations, Nicolae Ceaușescu's Communist dictatorship was overthrown, and Ion Iliescu took over as leader. Ceaușescu was deposed and fled the capital.
events.significance: Romania's revolution was the most violent of the 1989 uprisings against Communist rule in Eastern Europe. It ended decades of repressive rule.
